documents.unit: Division of Academic Affairs / AI @ UMD
documents.title: Guidelines for the Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) Tools at UMD
documents.stance_why: The guidelines say "It will be at the course instructor's discretion to determine whether GenAI may be used, to what extent, and for which assignments", so the document sets no single stance. It only gives students a fallback ("assume ... not allowed unless otherwise specified") and strongly encourages course policies, so delegates.
documents.summary: UMD's approved university-wide GenAI guidelines cover teaching and learning, research and administrative work. For courses they set a fallback that students assume AI is not allowed unless the syllabus says otherwise and leave the actual rule to instructors, with detector, privacy and tool-approval guidance.

units.why: The Purpose section says users "are encouraged to explore" GenAI "to enhance their teaching, learning, and work", a welcoming default, so P02 (permit or encourage by default) with a should modality.
units.anchor: encouraged to explore how generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools can enhance their teaching

units.why: Purpose statement of the framework: the guidelines aim "to promote transparency, enhance productivity, and uphold UMD's core values". This is an institution-level statement of purpose, so P56, informs.
units.anchor: promote transparency, enhance productivity, and uphold UMD's core values of integrity, inclusivity, and respect

units.why: The community is told it "expects" members to "follow these guidelines", a statement of scope and obligation of the framework, so P56 with should.
units.anchor: UMD expects its community members to follow these guidelines

units.why: Scope sentence defines who the guidelines bind ("all UMD faculty, staff, students, and affiliates"), so P61 (define scope).
units.anchor: apply to all UMD faculty, staff, students, and affiliates using GenAI tools and technologies

units.why: The scope names which tools are covered: "UMD-approved tools, publicly available/externally sourced platforms (free or paid)". This sets what the policy covers, so P61, not P07, because it is not about embedded editor tools.
units.anchor: They cover UMD-approved tools, publicly available/externally sourced platforms (free or paid)

units.why: "will be reviewed and updated regularly" is a commitment to revisit the guidance, so P54.
units.anchor: This guidance will be reviewed and updated regularly as technology and best practices evolve.

units.why: The Human Oversight principle says anyone using GenAI "should take full ownership of the resulting product", an accountability rule (P29) addressed to all users.
units.anchor: should take full ownership of the resulting product

units.why: Same principle: decisions "should not be based solely on outputs generated by GenAI tools", so humans must decide on consequential outcomes, P73 (not P46, which is grading only).
units.anchor: should not be based solely on outputs generated by GenAI tools

units.why: Access principle: "UMD will strive to address potential disparities in access or usage", an equity commitment, P51.
units.anchor: UMD will strive to address potential disparities in access or usage within our community

units.why: Privacy principle: use "should comply with" USM and UMD privacy policies and laws such as FERPA and HIPAA. Compliance with existing law and policy, so P77 rather than P50 (which is about protecting data and vetted tools).
units.anchor: should comply with the University System of Maryland (USM) and UMD data privacy policies
units.frag_start: The use of GenAI should comply

units.why: Transparency principle: all users "should disclose and, when applicable, make proper attribution" when using GenAI, so P24.
units.anchor: should disclose and, when applicable, make proper attribution when using GenAI tools

units.why: Accountability principle: users "are responsible for understanding the capabilities and limitations of GenAI tools". Closest is P31 (verify output) but the principle is about understanding limits generally.
units.anchor: responsible for understanding the capabilities and limitations of GenAI tools and ensuring appropriate use
units.fit_note: Requires understanding of tool capabilities and limitations and appropriate use, not specifically verifying each output.

units.why: The Acceptable Uses intro grounds the rules in integrity: GenAI content "presented as one's own work" compromises "intellectual honesty and scholarly integrity". This is a fairness/honesty reason, P95, not skill-building (P41).
units.anchor: presenting GenAI-generated content as one's own work

units.why: "should use UMD-approved GenAI tools, such as TerpAI when working and teaching on behalf of UMD" directs faculty, staff and student-employees to licensed tools, institution-wide, so P92 not P17.
units.anchor: such as TerpAI when working and teaching on behalf of UMD

units.why: "should not be used to fabricate, falsify, or misrepresent information, impersonate individuals, or generate deceptive content" is a general conduct ban on deceptive use, P74 (with a stated exception for controlled pedagogical or research purposes).
units.anchor: fabricate, falsify, or misrepresent information, impersonate individuals, or generate deceptive content
units.frag_start: GenAI tools should not be used

units.why: Warns that accepting "click-through agreements using UMD credentials" can mean "personal responsibility for compliance with the terms and conditions". This is about tool terms of use, nearest P52.
units.anchor: accepting click-through agreements using UMD credentials without delegated signature authority may result in personal responsibility
units.frag_end: terms and conditions of the AI tool.
units.fit_note: About personal liability for tool terms and click-through contracts, not copyright or ownership of outputs.

units.why: "UMD strongly recommends that all students utilize UMD-approved tools for study" directs students to licensed tools, institution-wide: P92.
units.anchor: UMD strongly recommends that all students utilize UMD-approved tools for study

units.why: "Instructors are strongly encouraged to establish a course-specific policy" asks instructors to have an AI policy for their course, P09.
units.anchor: Instructors are strongly encouraged to establish a course-specific policy
units.fit_note: Frames it as strongly encouraged, not mandatory.

units.anchor: that the use of GenAI tools to complete course assignments and assessments is not allowed

documents.stance_why: The page lists "Use of AI (Artificial Intelligence) tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Bing AI, etc.) for the completion of class work" among violations "that apply to all our courses", with no exception or permission route, so the department-level stance is prohibit, although it also tells students to read the syllabus for what is permissible.
documents.summary: The CS department integrity page lists AI tools used for class work among violations that apply to all its courses, and tells students to read each syllabus. The rest covers general integrity enforcement and consequences.

units.why: The page tells students that "For every CS course make sure you read the syllabus and understand what is permissible", so they must learn each course's rules, P78.

notes: Coder B. The CS page says to read the syllabus for what is permissible but lists AI use for class work as a violation applying to all courses; coded prohibit. Non-AI integrity items on the CS page (hardcoding, code sharing, similarity software) were not coded. Repeated sample-syllabus sentences in the TLTC page (email for exceptions, cite per assignment directions) were coded once.
